findings.issue: The record id is `doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42`, the DOI that resolves to the latest PhysioNet version, while the record declares `version: 3.1.0` and a `citation` whose DOI is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. The `doi` slot likewise carries 10.13026/37yb-1t42. A version-pinned record identified by a version-agnostic DOI is internally inconsistent: either the record refers to version 3.1.0 and should be identified by 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, or it refers to the dataset series and should not carry `version: 3.1.0`. The referent statement in `source_caveats` says the record describes the dataset 'at version 3.1.0', which favours the version-specific DOI.

Value is `https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/`, the Synapse controlled-access distribution point for the raw audio. The bundle presents Synapse as an access route for the raw audio (chunk c015/c018 news banner: 'Data will be made available via Synapse'), not as a resource this dataset was derived from. The released features were derived from the raw audio waveforms collected under the Bridge2AI-Voice protocol; naming the Synapse landing URL as the derivation source conflates a distribution endpoint with a provenance antecedent, and duplicates information already held in `raw_data_sources[0].access_details`.

`issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z'` is the publication date of version 3.1.0, which is consistent with `version: 3.1.0`, but conflicts with `id`/`doi` pointing at the version-agnostic latest-version DOI. This is the same identity inconsistency flagged for `id`; noted separately because the repair must keep `issued`, `version`, `citation` and the identifier slots referring to one and the same release.

`B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41` (Tab-separated values) is assigned to the participant-level instance. The substrate term is meant to describe the data substrate of the instance; a research participant's data in this release is carried across Parquet feature files and TSV phenotype tables, and the record itself states the phenotype tables are TSV while features are Parquet. Selecting TSV for the participant instance and Parquet (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30) for the recording instance encodes a file-format split rather than a property of the instance, and the bundle does not state that a participant instance is a TSV. Under the digest instruction to omit rather than approximate, this term is not clearly supported.

Only `timeframe_details` is populated ('The data were collected over a period of 12 months'), taken from the project documentation healthsheet. The bundle supports no start or end date for the dataset collection window, so `start_date`/`end_date` are correctly omitted; however the 12-month figure sits in tension with other bundle statements (IRB protocol describing a four-year study with phased collection begun November 2023 and ongoing November 2024; the feasibility study running June-July 2023). No caveat records this tension, whereas comparable tensions elsewhere in the record are caveated.

The final Creator entry carries no `principal_investigator`, only an affiliation named 'Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium' plus a `notes` string describing the consortium's size. Affiliation is declared as `Organization[]`; using it to stand in for an unnamed collective author, with the substantive content in `notes`, populates the object shape without populating the field the class declares for the creating party. The consortium is better recorded as the value it already occupies in `created_by`, which duplicates it.

`is_random` is omitted while `is_sample: true` and `is_representative: false` are set. The bundle states the sampling method explicitly ('Sampling Method: Non-Probability Sample', chunk c008), which supports `is_random: false`. This is a clearly supported omission.

Each DistributionFormat carries `access_urls` but no `download_url`, and the top-level `download_url` slot is also unpopulated. This is defensible — the bundle shows the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and the Files section states no direct download path — but the record nowhere states that no direct download URL exists, so a reader cannot distinguish deliberate omission from oversight. Low severity; omission is the safer answer and no repair is strictly required.

`examples` is populated with a single prose string rather than a list. The digest does not declare a range for `examples` on ExistingUse, so this may validate, but the sibling `intended_uses[*].examples` in the same record are emitted as lists. The inconsistent shaping of the same-named slot across two objects in one record is an internal inconsistency worth normalising.

The caveat correctly records that project documentation and PhysioNet disagree about whether free-speech transcripts are present in the release, and correctly prefers PhysioNet as higher-ranked. However the resolved fact — that free-speech transcripts and the spectrogram-family features derived from free speech were removed — is already stated in `known_limitations[3]` and `is_deidentified`, while the ContentWarning's own `warnings` list still asserts the protocol includes free speech tasks whose content cannot be fully controlled. That assertion is true of the collection protocol but the warning reads as applying to the released artifact, which per the preferred source no longer carries the free-speech text. The warning and its caveat point in opposite directions.

The `notes` slot carries the full AI-readiness rubric scoring (FAIRness 100%, characterization 80%, sustainability 50%, computability 75%, and the criterion-level pass/fail detail). This is bundle-supported content from chunk c009/c010, but the schema directs `notes` to residual content only, after every fitting slot is used. A self-assessment of the dataset against a readiness rubric is dataset commentary that `description` could hold, and the criterion-level failures (data quality not met, domain-appropriate not met, associated not met, contextualized not met) overlap `known_limitations`. Not a factual defect; a placement question.

`doi:10.13026/mf9s-5r03` is given as the pediatric dataset's identifier. The bundle (chunk c020) states this DOI as the pediatric project's latest-version DOI, while the version described in the accompanying `description` is 1.1.0, whose own DOI is 10.13026/h995-bt35. Same latest-version-versus-pinned-version mismatch as flagged for `id`, at lower stakes because the relationship is to the pediatric series as a whole.

The Bridge2AI-Voice FHIR profiles entry carries only a prose `external_resources` string with no URL, licence or archival flag, while every sibling entry carries at least a URL. The bundle (chunk c010) gives only 'B2Ai-Voice | FHIR — Description: FHIR profiles for voice as a biomarker' with a 'Navigate to Source Code' link whose target is not captured in the text, so no URL can be supplied. Correctly grounded; noted only because the entry is thinner than its siblings and adds little beyond naming the resource.

summary: Twelve findings against the full record; no fabrication or out-of-bundle content was detected, and no enum value outside the schema digest was used. The one high-severity finding is an identity inconsistency: the record is version-pinned to 3.1.0 with a 3.1.0 citation and a 1 May 2026 issuance, but is identified by the version-agnostic latest-version DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 in both `id` and `doi`; these must be brought into agreement, either by pinning the identifiers to 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 or by dropping the version pin. Two medium findings concern misplaced or unsupported values: `was_derived_from` names the Synapse controlled-access endpoint, which the bundle presents as a distribution route rather than a derivation antecedent and which duplicates `raw_data_sources[0].access_details`; and `instances[0].data_substrate` assigns Tab-separated values to the participant-level instance, a file-format distinction the bundle does not attach to that instance and which the digest instructs be omitted rather than approximated. One clearly supported omission was found: `sampling_strategies[0].is_random` should be false, given the bundle's explicit 'Sampling Method: Non-Probability Sample'. The remaining findings are low severity and mostly shape or placement: a Creator object standing in for the consortium with no `principal_investigator` and its substance in `notes`, duplicating `created_by`; `examples` emitted as prose on ExistingUse but as a list on IntendedUse; a ContentWarning whose `warnings` text and `source_caveats` pull in opposite directions about whether free-speech content survives in the release; the AI-readiness rubric occupying `notes` where `description` and `known_limitations` would fit it better; a latest-version rather than pinned DOI on the pediatric related dataset; a thin FHIR external resource; and an uncaveated tension between the stated 12-month collection window and the multi-year phased collection described in the IRB protocol. Sourcing discipline is otherwise sound: the existing `source_caveats` block correctly declares the referent, records the recording-count and consortium-size conflicts, and states which source was preferred and why.
